comparisons.peer_summary: The firm has minimal credit risk exposure from receivables from brokers, dealers, clearing organizations, and customers/counterparties, primarily due to their short-term nature, low probability of default, and collateralization. A table presents these other credit exposures, showing concentrations by industry, region, and internally determined public rating agency equivalents, while reflecting collateral considered in determining credit risk.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs discuss receivables within their balance sheet and risk disclosures, but they focus on different aspects: JPM explains a year-over-year decrease in accrued interest and accounts receivable driven by timing and client activities, whereas Goldman Sachs highlights the minimal credit risk associated with its receivables from brokers, dealers, and clearing organizations due to their short-term nature and collateralization.

sentences.text: Accrued interest and accounts receivable decreased primarily driven by lower receivables in Payments related to the timing of processing payment activities, due to December 31, 2023 falling on a weekend, as well as lower client receivables related to client-driven activities in Markets.
These receivables generally have minimal credit risk due to the low probability of clearing organization default and the short-term nature of receivables related to securities settlements.
